summary: A brutal economic engine-builder where you open burger, pizza, and sushi restaurants, hire and train staff, and blast the board with advertising to steer a fixed pool of customers to your tables. Turn order is earned rather than given, so a strong early lead compounds into a runaway win while late movers can be locked out entirely.
praised: no rubber-banding — good decisions actually snowball
huge variety of viable opening strategies
satisfying "aha" moment when an engine clicks
criticised: brutal to new players, especially in a 4-5p game
very long teach and long playtime
can feel solved/mathematical rather than thematic
a bad early game can be unwinnable by turn 3

interaction.kind: fighting over the same customers, streets and hiring/training order
interaction.detail: Every house's custom is shared and finite, so marketing, price wars and delivery routes exist specifically to steal customers from opponents before they can grab them. Being first to train an employee type means every future copy is free, so a huge part of strategy is denying opponents that training slot. Almost the entire map and customer base is contested common ground rather than a private board.
interaction.said: "cutthroat", "brutal", "one of the meanest games ever made", "not for the faint of heart"

subsystems: Single cash economy: hiring, training, marketing, and selling to grow revenue and cash on hand
scoring.how_you_win: Build and run a fast-food chain by hiring, training, marketing, and selling burgers and drinks; when the bank runs out of money for the second time the game ends and whoever holds the most cash wins, while running out of your own cash bankrupts and eliminates you first.

theme.said: 'the most thematic euro ever made,' 'you actually learn how a fast-food chain runs,' essentially never called pasted-on
theme.why: employees must be paid a wage every round whether or not they act, marketing only creates demand in houses that can see the billboard, and new hires must be trained by someone already possessing the skill, each mirroring a real business constraint rather than an abstract resource rule

style.why: A zero-luck economic engine of hiring, marketing and routes where players ruthlessly block and starve each other's businesses, but there is no direct attack, elimination, or asymmetric power
